item.title: Adani Ports to acquire Dutch operator Evos in €1.18 billion deal
item.description: The all-cash acquisition of Evos will give Adani Ports eight European terminals with 6.3 million cubic metres of storage capacity, expanding its liquid cargo portfolio.
item.dc:creator: Dhruvaksh Saha, Our Bureau
item.content:encoded: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone (APSEZ), India’s largest port operator, on Thursday said it would buy a 100 per cent stake in Netherlands-headquartered Evos B.V. (Evos) from Igneo Infrastructure Partners in an all-cash deal of €2.56 billion (₹27,142 crore). The transaction places Europe’s second-largest independent liquid-storage operator at an enterprise value of €2.56 billion (₹27,142 crore), APSEZ has informed the exchanges. The payment will be via debt and is subject to regulatory and other approvals and works council consultation. Evos has eight port-based terminals across key energy and industrial hubs in the Netherlands (Amsterdam East, Amsterdam West, Rotterdam and Terneuzen), Belgium (Ghent), Germany (Hamburg), Spain (Algeciras) and Malta. The European operator’s storage capacity is 6.3 million cubic metres and it provides essential infrastructure for the storage, handling and transshipment of liquid products, including gasoline, gasoil, marine fuels and jet fuel, alongside transition fuels such as sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), biofuels, methanol and bioethanol. For APSEZ, the move establishes a sizable European foothold, materially scales up and diversifies its liquids portfolio, and provides exposure to the long-term transition toward new-age fuels, it told the exchanges. “APSEZ intends to leverage its operating expertise and integrated logistics capabilities to strengthen the Target’s (Evos’) competitive position and support the long-term development of critical European trade infrastructure,” it said. According to Karan Adani, managing director of APSEZ, the move fits into the port operator’s target of handling 1 billion tonnes of cargo and building a global, integrated transport platform. Evos comprises 452 tanks, and 63 vessels and barge berths, and has several integrated pipeline connectivities (including Schiphol airport and Central Europe Pipeline System) and handled 37 million metric tonnes of throughput in 2025. Evos’ customers include energy majors, leading industrial and chemical companies, and commodity traders. According to APSEZ, its business model gives visibility of high revenues and cash flow, underpinned by tenured customer relationships, average 99 per cent commercial occupancy, and a substantial part of revenue under take-or-pay contracts and a CPI-linked contract base. “Importantly, Evos adds high-margin, predictable hard-currency cash flows backed by high take-or-pay revenues and CPI-linked contract base, strengthening the quality, resilience and geographic diversification of APSEZ’s earnings,” its statement said. Evos’ 56 per cent margin of earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation is above APSEZ’s H1FY27 “international ports” margin of 44.8 per cent. As of July-September, APSEZ had a cash balance of ₹12,502 crore. Japanese financier MUFG is the sole underwriter and has provided financing commitments for up to €2.8 billion for the proposed transaction. Linklaters and Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas have acted as international and domestic legal counsel for APSEZ, it said.

item.title: Airtel Q2 profit jumps 31%; spends ₹2,826 cr on data centre land purchase
item.description: Bharti Airtel's consolidated revenue rose 16.7% to ₹60,877.5 crore, while India mobile ARPU improved to ₹271 in Q2FY27 from ₹256 a year ago.
item.dc:creator: Gulveen Aulakh
item.content:encoded: India’s second-largest telecommunications (telecom) operator Bharti Airtel reported a 31 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y) rise in consolidated net profit at ₹8,887 crore, missing estimates for the second quarter of financial year 2026-27 (Q2FY27) due to rising network costs despite the addition of more high-paying premium customers. The figure was ₹6,791 crore in Q2FY26. Larger subscriber additions also reflected in revenues, which rose 16.7 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹60,887 crore, beating estimates. Sequentially, revenues rose 4 per cent from ₹58,539 crore in Q1FY27, while net profit increased from ₹8,167 crore. However, costs of network operation and maintenance rose 11 per cent to Rs 11,214 crore while licence fees rose 13 per cen to Rs 4,320 crore, pushing up expenses by 15 per cent to Rs 25,931 crore for the quarter.  Airtel spent ₹2,826 crore to acquire a strategic land parcel for its data-centre expansion, which will be one of its major growth levers going forward, along with financial services. “Our investment in a strategic land parcel during the quarter marks another important step towards realising our ambition of building 1 gigawatt (Gw) of data-centre capacity. In financial services, early traction following the commercial launch has been very encouraging, with our digital platforms, advanced data analytics, and disciplined operating model providing a strong foundation to scale the business. We continue to maintain a strong and resilient balance sheet, anchored by robust cash generation and disciplined capital allocation,” Bharti Airtel Executive Vice-Chairman Gopal Vittal said. The carrier’s India business reported a revenue of ₹42,308 crore in Q2FY27, up 9.4 per cent Y-o-Y from ₹38,690 crore, and up 2.7 per cent quarter-on-quarter (Q-o-Q) from ₹41,214 crore, driven by premiumisation of its mobile portfolio and strong momentum in its homes and enterprise businesses. India mobile revenue increased by 10.1 per cent Y-o-Y, led by higher Arpu (average revenue per user) and strong growth in smartphone data customer additions. Mobile services, which account for 73 per cent of total revenue, generated ₹30,943 crore. The telco’s net debt fell to ₹88,277 crore in Q2FY27 from ₹1.26 trillion a year earlier, excluding lease obligations. On an inclusive basis, net debt reduced to ₹1.6 trillion in Q2FY27 from ₹1.9 trillion in Q1FY27. The consolidated capex of the carrier, including India capex of ₹9,908 crore, stood at ₹12,467 crore for the quarter. Airtel’s Arpu, a key profitability metric for telecom operators, increased to ₹271 per month from ₹264 in Q1FY27, up 2.7 per cent. On a Y-o-Y basis, Arpu was up 5.9 per cent from ₹256 in Q2FY26. Airtel’s Arpu remained higher than Reliance Jio’s ₹218.8 per month. The increase was driven by strong net additions, particularly in the high-revenue postpaid segment, where Airtel added a record 1.2 million customers during the quarter, taking its total postpaid base to more than 31.2 million. “Our postpaid momentum remained strong with record-high net customer additions of 1.2 million. We added 2.9 million smartphone data customers, with continued improvement of our industry-leading Arpu at ₹271. The homes business saw 676,000 customer additions, driven by disciplined customer acquisition and continued progress on our convergence strategy,” Vittal said. Consolidated earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation (Ebitda) rose 17.8 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹35,240 crore in Q2FY27, beating estimates. India Ebitda stood at ₹25,729 crore. The consolidated Ebitda margin was 57.9 per cent, while the India Ebitda margin reached 60.8 per cent. Airtel’s India subscriber base rose 10.9 per cent Y-o-Y to more than 498.6 million as of September, remaining behind market leader Jio’s 542.2 million. Its smartphone data customer base grew by 18.8 million Y-o-Y to 304.6 million, accounting for 80 per cent of its total customer base. Its total customer base, including Africa, grew to 692.5 million. Average data consumption per customer on Airtel’s India network rose 28.8 per cent to 36.5 gigabyte (GB) in Q2FY27 from 28.3 GB in Q2FY26.

item.title: RBI proposes ₹100 crore limit on bank loans for agri infrastructure
item.description: The RBI has proposed a ₹100 crore aggregate loan limit per borrower for agricultural infrastructure under revised priority sector lending norms.
item.content:encoded:
Home / Industry / Banking / RBI proposes ₹100 crore limit on bank loans for agri infrastructure

RBI proposes ₹100 crore limit on bank loans for agri infrastructure The RBI has proposed a ₹100 crore aggregate loan limit per borrower for agricultural infrastructure under revised priority sector lending norms.

The Reserve Bank of India has proposed revised priority sector lending norms, including a ₹100 crore aggregate loan limit per borrower for agricultural infrastructure and higher eligibility limits for education and renewable energy loans. (Photo: Reuters)

Press Trust of India Mumbai 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 05 2026 | 11:16 PM IST

Listen to This Article

The Reserve Bank on Thursday proposed that loans for agricultural infrastructure will be subject to an aggregate sanctioned limit of Rs 100 crore per borrower from the banking system. As part of the ongoing effort towards consolidation of various instructions, the Reserve Bank of India said it has undertaken a review of the extant guidelines relating to Priority Sector Lending (PSL) and proposes to issue directions on the subject for different regulated entities, including commercial banks and regional rural banks. A draft direction on commercial banks proposed an aggregate loan limit of Rs 4 crore per borrowing entity for crop loans, medium and long-term loans for agriculture and allied activities, as well as loans for pre- and post-harvest activities.   It also said: "Loans for agriculture infrastructure will be subject to an aggregate sanctioned limit of Rs 100 crore per borrower from the banking system."   The lending to the agriculture sector will include farm credit (agriculture and allied activities), lending for agriculture infrastructure and ancillary activities. The draft further said that loans to individuals for educational purposes, including vocational courses, not exceeding Rs 25 lakh, will be considered as eligible for priority sector classification. Also Read

Regarding renewable energy, it said bank loans up to a limit of Rs 35 crore to borrowers for renewable energy-based power generators and for renewable energy-based public utilities -- street lighting systems, remote village electrification -- will be eligible for priority sector classification. For individual households, the loan limit will be Rs 10 lakh per borrower, the draft said. Agriculture, MSMEs, exports, education, housing, social infrastructure, and renewable energy are among the categories under the priority sector. The RBI has also issued separate draft directions for small finance banks, local area banks, and regional rural banks. RBI has invited comments and feedback on the drafts by November 26.

item.title: Saudi Arabia extends $3 billion financial support facility for Pakistan
item.description: Saudi Arabia has extended its $3 billion financing facility for Pakistan, while Islamabad is seeking loan rollovers from China and Kuwait to meet its external financing needs.
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / Saudi Arabia extends $3 billion financial support facility for Pakistan

Saudi Arabia extends $3 billion financial support facility for Pakistan Saudi Arabia has extended its $3 billion financing facility for Pakistan, while Islamabad is seeking loan rollovers from China and Kuwait to meet its external financing needs.

Saudi Arabia has extended its $3 billion financing facility for Pakistan, as Islamabad seeks further loan rollovers from China and Kuwait to meet about $21 billion in external debt repayment obligations during the current fiscal year. | Image: Reuter

Press Trust of India 4 min read Last Updated : Nov 05 2026 | 11:11 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Saudi Arabia has extended the USD 3 billion financing facility for Pakistan for a "reasonable period", according to Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb.   Saudi Arabia helped Pakistan with a USD 3 billion financing facility in April this year as Islamabad had to repay USD 3.5 billion to the United Arab Emirates. Initially, it was provided for three months.   "It has been extended, and for a reasonable period," Aurangzeb told journalists outside the Parliament on Wednesday.   "You don't need to worry as to for how long, given the kind of strategic relationship we have," Dawn quoted him as saying in response to a query that the financing facility had already matured on October 31.

Saudi Arabia had also provided another USD 5 billion to bridge the financing gap, and it had already been extended until 2028, Aurangzeb said. Also Read

Pakistan's economic rebound masks deeper problems despite market rally

US consortium pushes for $4.4 billion LNG project in Pakistan: Report

Carlyle Group, KKR get ready to snatch up bargain leveraged loans

Houthis deny drone attack on Saudi's Medina region, call claim fabricated

Air India, AI Express extend Saudi flight curbs till Nov 14 amid tensions

When asked if Pakistan had also sought additional support, the minister denied it, saying this was not needed as foreign exchange reserves covered more than three months of imports and would be strengthened to provide a four-month import cover by the end of the year through capital markets, according to Dawn.   Responding to another question about the prospects of the USD 10 billion Exchange Stabilisation Support Facility (ESSF) requested from the US in July this year, he sought to lower expectations that he himself had raised over the past several months.

"What we asked for back in July and were looking at was the market access. We have got the market access," he said, referring to the USD 3 billion bond Pakistan issued in September against orders worth USD 6 billion.   "If that (ESSF) materialises, fantastic, it will be a liquidity support facility.   Otherwise, we have plans for further Eurobond issuance, Panda bond issuance and rupee-linked dollar-settled bond," the minister said.   He added that he had held meetings with 70-80 institutional investors in Bangkok, who had a very clear view of Pakistan, and that offers were available for five-year and 10-year maturities, "because clearly we are looking beyond the [IMF] programme".

He said the government was looking at the US from a broader perspective, as the US Export-Import Bank and Development   Finance Corporation (DFC) needed to support their investors and exporters in Pakistan. "That is real financing and real credit," he said, adding that the ESSF request was for a liquidity support facility to help the sovereign.   "If possible, fine; if not, we are going to move forward, with or without it." The finance minister also reported that the International Monetary Fund (IMF) Executive Board meeting to approve a disbursement of USD 1.2 billion to Pakistan would be held in December.   Earlier, he told the Senate Standing Committee on Finance that Pakistan was targeting a reduction of USD 4 billion in external debt during the current fiscal year and USD 3.5 billion next year, compared with USD 4.5 billion in the last fiscal year.

He said the government was seeking to replace expensive short-term borrowing with longer-maturity financing through bonds and private placements to reduce refinancing risks.   He said external debt had been rising by USD 5-6 billion annually, from USD 45 billion in 2014-15 to around USD 100 billion, but had increased by only USD 1 billion annually over the past two years, according to Dawn.   Meanwhile, sources in the finance ministry said that Pakistan is also negotiating with China and Kuwait to roll over loans worth USD 4.3 billion in a bid to supportÂ the country's external financing requirements during the 2026/27 fiscal year.

Pakistan is also close to getting approval from China to roll over USD 4 billion in loans and a rollover of USD 300 million from Kuwait, they said.   According to the sources, the USD 4 billion Chinese loan is expected to be rolled over in March 2027.Â  Pakistan is scheduled to secure total debt rollovers of USD 7.3 billion from Saudi Arabia, China, and Kuwait for one year.   The rollover arrangements are part of Pakistan's external financing strategy for the current fiscal year, during which the country faces external debt repayment obligations of approximately USD 21 billion.   The expected USD 7.3 billion in rollovers is included in these obligations.
